title: Mold Remediation Clearance Standard
content:
On a Mold Remediation job, clearance is requested once the supervisor reports remediation complete. The job must be in awaiting clearance status when a clearance result is recorded. Clearance is established by the tier's clearance method, and the result is recorded exactly as the clearance report states it, numbered by attempt from 1: a pass moves the job to cleared, and a fail returns it to remediation for re-cleaning.

Only the first clearance attempt's fee is billed. The fee passed through is the tier's clearance test fee, and on supervisor visual inspection tiers that fee is 0.00 and no fee line is booked. Retests after a failed clearance are at the company's cost on every tier. A job that has failed the tier's maximum number of clearance attempts is handed to a human project manager as not covered by policy.

## Recording a result

| Clearance report states | Attempt number | Job moves to |
|---|---|---|
| Pass | Next number in sequence from 1 | Cleared |
| Fail | Next number in sequence from 1 | Remediating, for re-cleaning |

The job's status must read awaiting clearance on the company's records when the result is recorded.

## Fee by attempt

| Attempt | Fee line |
|---|---|
| 1, on an independent assessor verification tier | The tier's clearance test fee |
| 1, on a supervisor visual inspection tier | None; the fee is 0.00 |
| 2 or later | None; the retest is at the company's cost |

Whether an attempt is the first is read from its attempt number on the clearance records.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A job on a tier with a maximum of 3 clearance attempts fails attempts 1, 2 and 3. Only attempt 1 carried a fee line. After the third failure the job has failed the tier's maximum and is handed to a human project manager as not covered by policy.
